unruh_effect.goal: An observer accelerating at a through empty space sees it filled with thermal radiation. Write its temperature T, from ħ, the speed of light c and Boltzmann's constant k.
unruh_effect.name: Unruh temperature
unruh_effect.ask: Find T in kelvin for a = 2.47e20 m/s² (h = 1.0546e-34 for ħ, c = 2.998e8, k = 1.381e-23).
unruh_effect.method: The accelerated observer's horizon sits a distance c²/a behind them; seen from their frame the vacuum modes are thermal at that horizon's surface gravity.

hawking_radiation.goal: A black hole of mass M glows as a black body. Write its temperature T, from ħ, c, gravity's constant G and Boltzmann's k.
hawking_radiation.name: Hawking temperature of a mass
hawking_radiation.ask: Find T in kelvin for M = 1e12 kg (h = 1.0546e-34 for ħ, c = 2.998e8, G = 6.674e-11, k = 1.381e-23).
hawking_radiation.method: The surface gravity of a Schwarzschild horizon is κ = c⁴/4GM; put it in kT = ħκ/2πc.

black_hole_thermodynamics.goal: A horizon of area A carries an entropy S, counted in units of Boltzmann's constant, set only by c, G and ħ. Write S.
black_hole_thermodynamics.name: Bekenstein-Hawking entropy
black_hole_thermodynamics.ask: Find S in units of 10⁷⁰ k (u = 1e70) for a solar-mass hole, A = 1.096e8 m² (c = 2.998e8, G = 6.674e-11, h = 1.0546e-34 for ħ).
black_hole_thermodynamics.method: Integrate dS = dE/T with E = Mc² and the Hawking temperature: S grows as M², which is the area.

information_paradox.goal: A black hole of mass M evaporates completely in a time t that grows as the cube of its mass, from G, ħ and c. Write t.
information_paradox.name: Evaporation time
information_paradox.ask: Find t in billions of years (u = 3.156e16 s) for M = 1e11 kg (G = 6.674e-11, h = 1.0546e-34 for ħ, c = 2.998e8).
information_paradox.method: Power radiated goes as 1/M² (Stefan-Boltzmann at T ∝ 1/M over an area ∝ M²); dM/dt ∝ −1/M² integrates to t ∝ M³.

loop_quantum_gravity.goal: Where a spin network's link of spin j crosses a surface it gives that surface an area A, in units of the Planck area l, scaled by the Immirzi parameter γ. Write A.
loop_quantum_gravity.name: Quantised geometry
loop_quantum_gravity.ask: Find A in Planck areas for the smallest step, j = 0.5, with g = 0.2375 for γ.
loop_quantum_gravity.method: The area operator acts on each link like the length of an angular momentum: its eigenvalues are √(j(j+1)).

causal_set_theory.goal: Events are scattered at random with density ρ through spacetime. Write the chance P that a region of volume V holds none at all.
causal_set_theory.name: Poisson sprinkling
causal_set_theory.ask: Find P for p = 0.5 events per unit volume in a region of V = 3.
causal_set_theory.method: A Poisson process with mean ρV gives n events with probability (ρV)ⁿe^(−ρV)/n!; put n = 0.

er_epr.goal: Each maximally entangled pair of qubits shares one unit of entanglement entropy. Write the entropy S of n such pairs, in nats.
er_epr.name: Bell-pair counting
er_epr.method: Each half of a Bell pair is in a mixed state, ½ and ½: its entropy is −Σ p ln p = ln 2.

asymptotic_safety.goal: Newton's constant G, probed at momentum k, weakens with a coefficient ω. Write the dimensionless strength g = G k² it runs to.
asymptotic_safety.name: Running coupling
asymptotic_safety.ask: Find g for G = 1, k = 10, w = 1.414 (it approaches the fixed point 1/w as k grows).
asymptotic_safety.method: Solve the renormalisation-group equation dg/d ln k = 2g − 2ωg² - it flows to g* = 1/ω.

page_curve.goal: A black hole takes a time τ to evaporate from mass M to nothing, its remaining lifetime going as the cube of its mass. Write the time t it takes to shrink from M to m.
page_curve.name: Page time
page_curve.ask: Find t in billions of years for T = 10, M = 1 and m = 0.7071 (half the entropy gone: m = M/√2).
page_curve.method: The time left goes as M³, so the time taken to fall to m is τ − τ(m/M)³. Entropy goes as M², so half is gone at m = M/√2.

ads_cft.goal: Gravity in a three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space of radius L, with gravity's constant G, is the same as a two-dimensional conformal field theory whose central charge C counts its degrees of freedom. Write C.
ads_cft.name: Brown-Henneaux relation
ads_cft.ask: Find C for L = 1000 and G = 1 (in Planck units).
ads_cft.method: The asymptotic symmetries of AdS₃ form two Virasoro algebras whose central charge comes out as 3L/2G.
